meaning: result, outcome; (between clauses) and in the end, as it turned out

senses.en: result; outcome (检查结果 'test results')
and in the end; as it turned out: introduces what actually happened, often not what was hoped

examples.en: Doctor, how are the test results?
examples.analysis: 结果 is a noun here, the head of 检查结果 'test results': the first noun describes the second with no 的 needed. 怎么样? 'how is it?' asks for an overall verdict. 医生 at the start just addresses the doctor.

examples.zh: 我等了他一个小时，结果他没来。
examples.en: I waited an hour for him, and in the end he didn't show up.
examples.analysis: 结果 opens the second clause and reports how things actually turned out, here a let-down after the effort in the first clause. It works like 'and in the end'. 等了他一个小时: the length of time, 一个小时, comes after the verb and its object.

examples.en: So how did it end? Did you go?
examples.analysis: Said while listening to someone's story: 结果呢? = 'and the outcome?', a nudge to get to the end. 那 'so, then' ties it to what was just said; a noun + 呢 asks about that thing. 你们去了吗? then asks for the detail.

collocations.en: so how did it turn out?

related.en: finally; last in a sequence; 结果 puts the stress on the outcome
afterwards; later on (in a past story)
cause; reason (what led to the result)

meaning: to be careful; to watch out (for); careful

senses.en: to be careful; watch out! (said alone as a warning)
to watch out for (小心 + danger: 小心车 'mind the cars')
careful, cautious in how one acts (开车很小心)

examples.en: Watch out! There's a car coming!
examples.analysis: Shouted on its own, 小心! is the everyday warning, 'Careful!' or 'Watch out!'. 车来了 then names the danger: 来了 'is coming', with 了 marking a new situation that has just arisen.

examples.en: It's snowing. Be careful on the way.
examples.analysis: 路上小心 'careful on the way' is the standard send-off to someone heading out. 路上 'on the road' comes first and sets where to be careful. 下雪了: 了 marks a new situation, 'it has started snowing'.

examples.en: He's a careful driver.
examples.analysis: 小心 works as an adjective here, so it takes 很: the activity 开车 'driving' comes right after the subject, and 很小心 comments on it. English puts the same idea as 'drives carefully' or 'a careful driver'.

collocations.en: be careful; take a bit more care

related.en: conscientious; serious about doing it right
to feel at ease; stop worrying

meaning: at that time; then (a past moment already clear from context)

senses.en: at that time; then: a time word for a past moment already mentioned
当时的 + noun: … of that time (当时的天气 'the weather then')

examples.zh: 我当时不知道他是你哥哥。
examples.en: I didn't know at the time that he was your brother.
examples.analysis: 当时 sits after the subject and before the verb, a normal place for time words: 我 + 当时 + 不知道. It points back to a past moment already clear from context. 知道 is negated with 不 here even though the moment is past.

examples.en: Where were you at the time?
examples.analysis: Here 当时 opens the sentence, before the subject, to set the scene first: 'at that moment, where were you?'. Chinese has no past tense; the time word alone places the question in the past.

examples.zh: 当时太忙了，忘了给你打电话。
examples.en: I was so busy then that I forgot to call you.
examples.analysis: An apology: 当时 places the busyness at the moment in question. 太忙了 'so busy', then 忘了 + 给你打电话 'forgot to call you'. The subject 'I' is left out because it is obvious who is speaking.

collocations.en: of that time (当时的想法 'what one thought then')

related.en: back then; can cover a longer stretch, like years
before; in the past
now

meaning: or (in statements); the short, more formal form of 或者

senses.en: or: joins two options in a statement (今天或明天 'today or tomorrow')

examples.zh: 打电话或发短信都可以。
examples.en: You can call or text, either is fine.
examples.analysis: 或 joins two options, 打电话 'call' and 发短信 'text'; 都可以 'either is fine' then covers both. 或 is the short, slightly formal form of 或者; in casual talk most people say 或者 here.

examples.zh: 下午三点或四点，你看呢？
examples.en: Three or four in the afternoon. What do you think?
examples.analysis: Proposing a meeting time: 或 links two clock times in a suggestion. 你看呢? 'how about it?' hands the choice to the listener. To ask 'which one, three or four?', Chinese uses 还是 instead: 三点还是四点?

examples.zh: 今天或明天告诉我就行。
examples.en: Just let me know today or tomorrow.
examples.analysis: 今天或明天 'today or tomorrow' opens the sentence as the time frame. 告诉我 'tell me' is the request, and 就行 'that will do' at the end makes it easygoing: that is all the speaker needs.

collocations.en: either A or B is fine

related.en: or; same meaning, more common in speech
or, in questions asking which one (茶还是咖啡？)

meaning: to understand; to know about (a subject)

senses.en: to understand (what someone means or says)
to know about, be good with (懂电脑 'know computers')
after a verb, the result 'understood': 听懂 'catch (by ear)', 看懂 'make sense of'

examples.en: Do you get what I mean?
examples.analysis: 懂 takes the thing understood as its object: 懂 + 我的意思 'my meaning'. 吗 turns it into a yes/no question; the short answers are just 懂 or 不懂.

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't catch that.
examples.analysis: Here 懂 follows the verb 听 'listen' and gives its result: 听懂 = 'listen and understand'. 没 + 听懂 says the listening happened but understanding didn't. A line worth having ready in any conversation.

examples.en: He knows a lot about computers. Ask him.
examples.analysis: 懂 + a field = 'know about': 懂电脑 'know computers'. Because this 懂 describes knowledge someone has, it can take 很 like 喜欢 does: 很懂 'really knows'. 吧 turns 你问他 into a suggestion.

related.en: to understand; clear (often about a situation or an explanation)
to know (a fact); 懂 is about grasping meaning
to understand, know (a principle; a bit more formal)

hook: 忄 'heart, mind' on the left marks a mental act; 董 dǒng on the right gives the sound.

meaning: what should I/we do?; what to do (about a problem)

senses.en: what should I/we do? (asking for a way out of a problem)
inside a sentence: what to do (不知道怎么办 'don't know what to do')

examples.en: I forgot to bring my passport. What do I do?
examples.analysis: 怎么办 after a problem asks 'what should I do?'. It is a full question by itself and needs no 吗. 忘带 + object + 了 = 'forgot to bring …': 了 at the end reports the new, unwelcome situation.

examples.en: I don't know what to do either.
examples.analysis: Here 怎么办 is the object of 不知道: 'don't know what to do'. Inside a statement it no longer asks anything, so the sentence ends with a full stop. 也 'also, either' echoes someone else's worry.

examples.en: What if it rains tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 如果 + situation, then 怎么办? = 'what do we do if …?', a common way to say 'what if …?' when raising a problem. Useful for raising a backup plan before an outing or an event.

collocations.en: so what do I do? (thinking aloud)

related.en: way; method (没办法 'there's nothing to be done')
to do; to handle
how; why

meaning: to tell (a story); to explain; to talk about

senses.en: to tell; to talk about (讲故事 'tell a story')
to explain; to teach (讲得很清楚 'explains clearly')
to speak (a language), like 说: 讲中文

examples.zh: 你给我讲讲昨天的事吧。
examples.en: Tell me about what happened yesterday.
examples.analysis: 给我讲讲 = 'tell me about it': 给 + person marks who hears it, and doubling the verb, 讲讲, makes the request light, 'tell me a bit'. 昨天的事 'yesterday's matter' is the object; 吧 softens it further.

examples.zh: 他讲得很清楚，我一听就懂了。
examples.en: He explained it really clearly; I got it right away.
examples.analysis: 讲 here is 'to explain'. Verb + 得 + comment says how it was done: 讲得很清楚 'explained very clearly'. 一听就懂了 'understood as soon as I heard it' uses 一 … 就 … 'as soon as … then …'.

examples.en: Stop talking. I don't want to hear it.
examples.analysis: 别 + verb + 了 = 'stop doing that': 别讲了 'stop talking about it'. 讲 here is simply 'talk about something'; 别说了 would mean the same. 我不想听 'I don't want to hear it' gives the reason.

collocations.en: teach a class; give a lecture
to speak; to give a talk

related.en: to say; to speak (the general word)
to tell (someone a piece of information)

meaning: to choose; to pick; to elect

senses.en: to choose; to pick (from options)
to elect; to vote someone in (选他当组长)

examples.en: Of these two, which one would you pick?
examples.analysis: The options come first as the topic, 这两个 'these two', then 你选哪个? 'which do you pick?'. 选 takes 哪个 'which one' as its object; no 吗 is needed because the question word does the asking.

examples.en: Help me pick something to wear.
examples.analysis: 帮我 + verb = 'do … for me': 帮我选 'help me choose'. 一件衣服 is what is being picked, with 件 as the measure word for clothes. 吧 makes it a friendly request rather than an order.

examples.en: Everyone picked him as team leader.
examples.analysis: 选 + person + 当 + role = 'choose someone to be …': 选他当组长. 当 dāng means 'to serve as'. This is 选 as 'elect, vote in', here within a small team.

collocations.en: finish choosing (你选好了吗？ 'Have you decided?')
to get picked; to be elected

related.en: to choose; a choice (more formal; also a noun)
to want; to take (when ordering or buying)

meaning: to feel (an emotion or a physical state)

senses.en: to feel (+ a feeling or state: 感到很累 'feel very tired')
让 + person + 感到 …: to make someone feel …

examples.en: Have you been feeling very tired lately?
examples.analysis: 有没有 + verb? asks 'have you or haven't you…?'. With 感到 + a state it asks about a symptom, the way a doctor might. 最近 'lately' up front sets the time frame; the 'you' is understood.

examples.zh: 我对这个结果感到很满意。
examples.en: I'm very happy with this result.
examples.analysis: 对 + thing + 感到 + feeling = 'feel … about something': 对这个结果感到很满意 'feel satisfied with this result'. 对 names what the feeling is about and comes before 感到. A typical line at work or after a test; in casual chat people also just say 我很满意.

examples.zh: 这件事让我感到很难过。
examples.en: This made me very sad.
examples.analysis: 让 + person + 感到 + feeling = 'make someone feel …': 让我感到很难过 'made me feel very sad'. 件 is the measure word for 事 'matter'. This 让…感到 frame is a very common home for 感到.

related.en: to feel; to think (more casual; also for opinions)
to feel; a feeling (also a noun)

meaning: story; tale

senses.en: story (told or read): 讲故事 'tell a story'
someone's story: what happened to a person

examples.en: Mom, tell me one more story!
examples.analysis: 故事 is the object of 讲 'tell': 讲故事 is the standard pairing, and the measure word is 个. 再 'again, one more' + 吧 makes it a coaxing request; with 妈妈 at the start it sounds like a child asking for another story.

examples.en: Have you heard this story?
examples.analysis: The object, 这个故事, moves to the front as the topic; then 你听过吗? 'have you heard (it)?'. 过 after 听 marks experience, 'ever heard'.

examples.zh: 他讲的故事都很有意思。
examples.en: The stories he tells are all really interesting.
examples.analysis: 他讲的 'that he tells' describes 故事 through 的. 故事 itself does not change for plural; 都 'all' shows the speaker means several stories.

related.en: novel; fiction (written)
joke
to tell (讲故事)

meaning: to change; to swap; to exchange (money)

senses.en: to change, swap one thing for another (换衣服, 换工作)
to exchange (换钱 'change money')
to switch (vehicles, times, places): 换车 'change buses or trains'

examples.zh: 不用换衣服，这样就很好。
examples.en: No need to change. You look fine like this.
examples.analysis: 不用 + verb = 'there's no need to': 不用换衣服 'no need to change (clothes)'; 换衣服 is the standard phrase for changing outfits. 这样 'like this' + 就很好 'is just fine' reassures the listener.

examples.en: Where can I change money?
examples.analysis: 换钱 = 'change money', one currency into another. The place question 在哪儿 comes before the verb, where location phrases go in Chinese; 可以 'can' asks where it is possible to do this.

examples.en: Could we do it at another time?
examples.analysis: 能不能 + verb? politely asks 'could we …?'. 换 + (一)个 + noun means 'switch to a different one': 换个时间 'another time'. The sentence has no separate word for 'another'; 换 'switch' carries that idea.

related.en: to change, become different; 换 replaces one thing with another
to alter; to correct

hook: 扌 'hand' on the left; 奂 huàn on the right gives the sound.

meaning: we; us (you and me both: includes the listener)

senses.en: we; us, including the person spoken to (common in the north)

examples.en: Let's go.
examples.analysis: 咱们 + verb + 吧 = 'let's …'. 咱们 includes the listener, so it fits suggestions for the two of you or the whole group. 我们走吧 also works; 咱们 sounds a little warmer and more colloquial.

examples.en: What time shall we meet tomorrow?
examples.analysis: Time words go before the verb: 咱们 + 明天 + 几点 + 见. 几点 'what time' asks the clock time. 咱们 here is 'you and me', so the question treats the plan as shared.

examples.en: Let's not wait for him any more.
examples.analysis: 咱们 + 别 + verb + 了 = 'let's stop …'. 了 marks a change of plan: we were waiting, now we stop. Because 咱们 includes the listener, this is a proposal to them, not a report about the speaker.

related.en: we; us (may or may not include the listener)
short form of 咱们
everyone

meaning: to be under way; to carry out (an activity); formal in tone

senses.en: (of an event or plan) to be under way; to go (进行得很顺利 'go smoothly')
to carry out (进行 + action noun: 进行检查 'do an examination')

examples.en: Is the event still going on?
examples.analysis: 进行 here means 'be under way'. 在 before the verb marks an ongoing action, and 还 'still' asks if it has not yet ended. The subject is the event itself, 活动.

examples.zh: 我们的计划进行得不太顺利。
examples.en: Our plan isn't going very smoothly.
examples.analysis: 进行 + 得 + comment says how something is going: 进行得不太顺利 'not going very smoothly'. 不太 'not very' softens the bad news. A typical line in a work update.

examples.zh: 下周要进行一次全身检查。
examples.en: There's a full checkup next week.
examples.analysis: 进行 + action noun = 'carry out …': 进行检查 'carry out an examination', with 一次 'one round' in between. 进行 gives a formal, official tone; in casual speech people would say 做检查.

related.en: to do (the everyday word: 做检查)
to hold (a meeting, a ceremony)

meaning: measure word for a stretch: of time, road, speech or text

senses.en: a period of time: 一段时间 'a while', 这段时间 'lately'
a stretch of road or distance: 一段路
a passage of speech, text or music: 一段话

examples.zh: 我最近这段时间特别忙。
examples.en: I've been really busy lately.
examples.analysis: 段 measures a stretch of time: 这段时间 'this period'. Together with 最近 'recently' it means 'lately, these days'. 特别 'really, extremely' makes 忙 stronger.

examples.zh: 前边那段路不好走，开慢一点儿。
examples.en: That stretch of road ahead is rough. Drive a bit slower.
examples.analysis: 那段路 'that stretch of road': 段 marks off one section of something long. 不好走 'hard to travel on'. 开慢一点儿 'drive a little slower': adjective + 一点儿 after the verb makes a gentle request.

examples.en: What does this passage mean?
examples.analysis: 段 measures a piece of speech or writing: 这段话 'this passage, these few lines'. 是什么意思? 'what does it mean?'. Handy when reading a message or a document with someone.

collocations.en: a period of time; a while

related.en: the general measure word
part; section
measure word for times, occurrences

meaning: just; only a moment ago; (刚刚好) exactly, just right

senses.en: just, a moment ago (刚刚 + verb)
exactly, just enough (刚刚好 'just right')

examples.en: I just got here. Where are you?
examples.analysis: 刚刚 sits right before the verb: 我 + 刚刚 + 到 'I've just arrived'. It stresses that it happened only moments ago, and the sentence needs no 了 to show it is done.

examples.zh: 他刚刚出去，一会儿就回来。
examples.en: He's just stepped out. He'll be back in a moment.
examples.analysis: 刚刚 + 出去 'has just gone out'. The second clause, 一会儿就回来, means 'will be back shortly': 一会儿 'a little while' + 就 'then'. A typical reply when someone asks for a colleague.

examples.zh: 这件衣服不大不小，刚刚好。
examples.en: This piece of clothing is not too big and not too small. It's just right.
examples.analysis: 刚刚好 = 'just right': here 刚刚 means 'exactly' rather than 'a moment ago'. 不大不小 'neither big nor small' sets it up. You'll hear it about sizes, amounts and timing.

related.en: just now (a time word; can open the sentence)
just (the one-syllable form, right before the verb)
already

meaning: to act, take action; action; to move about (get around)

senses.en: to move about, get around (行动不方便 'has trouble getting around')
to act; to take action
action (as opposed to words)

measure.note: 一次行动 'one operation or action' (次 counts occasions; 个 also works)

examples.zh: 我奶奶腿疼，行动不方便。
examples.en: My grandma's legs hurt, so she has trouble getting around.
examples.analysis: 行动 here is moving about, said of the body, and it is the subject of 不方便 'not easy'. 行动不方便 is a common, polite way to say someone has limited mobility. 腿疼 'legs hurt' gives the reason.

examples.en: Stop waiting. Act now!
examples.analysis: 行动 as a verb: 'take action, get going'. 马上 'right away' sits before it, and 吧 makes it a push rather than an order. 别等了 'stop waiting' sets up the contrast between waiting and doing.

examples.zh: 他说得很好，可是没有行动。
examples.en: He said all the right things, but didn't follow through.
examples.analysis: Here 行动 means acting on one's words: 没有行动 'there was no action' (he did not act). 说得很好 'spoke well' and 没有行动 set words against deeds; 可是 'but' marks the turn.

related.en: to move
activity; to move about, exercise
to do

meaning: hard-working; to make an effort; (努力 + verb) to work hard at

senses.en: hard-working; putting in effort (他很努力)
to try hard; to do one's best (我会努力的)
努力 + verb: do something hard (努力工作 'work hard')

examples.en: He works really hard.
examples.analysis: 努力 is an adjective here, so it takes 很: the topic 工作 'work' comes after the subject, and 很努力 comments on it. English turns the same idea into 'works hard'.

examples.zh: 别太累了，你已经很努力了。
examples.en: Don't wear yourself out. You've already tried so hard.
examples.analysis: 已经很努力了 'have already tried very hard': 已经 'already' + 很努力 + 了, which presents it as a state that has been reached. Said to comfort someone who feels they are falling short. 别太累了 'don't overdo it'.

examples.en: I'll do my best.
examples.analysis: 会 … 的 frames a firm promise: 'I will, for sure'. 努力 works as a verb here, 'make an effort', with no object. The usual reply when someone encourages you.

related.en: conscientious; careful to do it right
come on! keep going! (cheering someone's effort)

meaning: alcohol; an alcoholic drink (wine, spirits, beer: context decides)

senses.en: alcohol; an alcoholic drink in general (喝酒 'drink')
liquor or wine of a particular kind, when context makes it clear

measure.note: 一杯酒 'a glass of wine'; 瓶 for a bottle

examples.en: I'm driving, so I can't drink.
examples.analysis: 喝酒 'drink alcohol' is verb + object; 酒 covers any alcoholic drink, so 喝酒 is the plain way to say 'drink' in this sense. 不能 'can't' states the rule; the first clause gives the reason without a word for 'so'.

examples.en: Do you usually drink?
examples.analysis: A doctor's history question: 平时 'usually, normally' before the verb asks about habit, and 喝酒 means drinking alcohol. 吗 makes it yes/no. The answer is often 喝 or 不喝, or a hedge such as 喝一点 'a little'.

examples.en: How much is this bottle of wine?
examples.analysis: 瓶 'bottle' is the measure word: 这 + 瓶 + 酒 'this bottle of …'. 酒 alone does not say which kind; English has to choose 'wine', 'liquor' or 'beer' from context. 多少钱? 'how much?'.

related.en: hotel (not a bar)
cheers! (literally 'dry the glass')
tea

hook: 氵 'water' on the left; 酉 on the right began as a picture of a wine jar.

meaning: to send (a message, photo, email); to hand out; to break out

senses.en: to send (a text, a photo, an email): 发短信
to hand out; to issue (发工资 'pay wages')
(of the body) to develop, break out: 发烧 'have a fever'

examples.en: Text me when you get there.
examples.analysis: 给 + person + 发 + message = 'send someone …': 给我发个短信 'send me a text'. 个 with 一 dropped makes it casual, 'a quick text'. 到了 at the start sets the time: 'once you've arrived'.

examples.en: Send me the photos.
examples.analysis: The thing being sent comes first as the topic, 照片 'the photos', then 发给我 'send to me': 给 right after the verb marks the receiver. 吧 keeps the request casual.

examples.en: Did you send it? I didn't get it.
examples.analysis: 发 here has no object: both people know what was sent, an email or a file. 发了吗? 'have you sent it?', with 了 for completion. 没收到 'haven't received' is the other end of 发.

related.en: to receive (the other end of 发)
to deliver; to give as a gift; to see someone off

meaning: just now; a moment ago (a time word)

senses.en: just now, a few moments ago: a time word that can open the sentence
刚才的 + noun: the … from a moment ago (刚才的事)

examples.en: Who called me just now?
examples.analysis: 刚才 is a time word, so it can open the sentence, before the subject 谁 'who'. 给我打电话 'phone me', and 了 at the end marks the call as having happened.

examples.en: Sorry about what happened just now.
examples.analysis: 刚才 + 的 describes a noun: 刚才的事 'what happened a moment ago'. Putting it first as the topic and then saying 对不起 is a natural way to apologize for a scene or a sharp remark.

examples.zh: 你刚才说什么？我没听清楚。
examples.en: What did you just say? I didn't catch it.
examples.analysis: Here 刚才 sits between the subject and the verb: 你 + 刚才 + 说. 听清楚 'hear clearly' is listen + result; with 没 it means the words didn't come through.

related.en: just (adverb; also 'exactly' in 刚刚好)
just (adverb, right before the verb)
now
